notes:
I've written notes for most of Colossians 2. Two verses are thin: v. 18 has one point and v. 19 has none. My searches didn't find any Lutheran, Methodist, Orthodox, bibleodyssey.org, netbible.org or prosperity/hyper-grace material on this chapter, so those views are left out.

---

**v. 1**
- Guzik says the "conflict" was inside Paul, not a fight with other people. It was his spiritual struggle and deep care for believers he had never met. https://enduringword.com/great-conflict/ 
- Guzik ties it to the athletic language of 1:29, and to prayer, which he calls the heart of the struggle. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/colossians-2/
- Matthew Henry says Paul was "in a sort of agony" and afraid for them, following Christ's example. He adds that believers can share fellowship with churches they have never met. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Col/Col_002.cfm 

**v. 2**
- Guzik sees three concerns: their courage ("encouraged" meant fit to face hardship), their unity (built by love, not force) and their understanding. He quotes Wuest that "the mystery is Christ." https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/colossians-2/
- Henry notes that Paul prays for comforted hearts, not health or wealth. He calls the soul's prosperity "the best prosperity." This is Henry's own remark; he isn't responding to modern prosperity teaching. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Col/Col_002.cfm 

**v. 3**
- The false teachers told people to look for wisdom somewhere other than Jesus. Paul replies that all of it is found in Him. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/colossians-2/ 
- Guzik cites Barclay: "hidden" (*apokruphos*) was a jab at Gnostic secret books. Vaughn adds that it means "stored up," not "concealed." https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/colossians-2/
- Henry: the treasures are hidden "not from us, but for us," in Christ. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Col/Col_002.cfm 

**v. 4**
- The "deeper wisdom" teachers were persuasive, and talk of hidden knowledge can be both attractive and misleading. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/colossians-2/  Paul doesn't say they had already been fooled, only that the danger was real. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/colossians-2/
- Henry says Satan ruins people by deceiving them, and his agents use flattering words to do it. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Col/Col_002.cfm 

**v. 5**
- Through prayer, Paul felt truly present with them. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/colossians-2/ 
- Vaughn reads "order" and "firm" as military words: an army under attack whose lines still hold. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/colossians-2/ 
- Henry: the "communion of saints is a spiritual thing." https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Col/Col_002.cfm 

**v. 6**
- F.F. Bruce, quoted by Guzik: "received" is the word for receiving something handed down. The Colossians received Christ himself as their "tradition," which guards them against the "tradition of men" in v. 8. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/colossians-2/ 
- Guzik: you received Jesus by simple faith and by grace, so keep walking the same way. https://enduringword.com/walking-rooted-building/ 

**v. 7**
- Guzik: Paul mixes pictures (walking, rooted, built up), but the point is simple: be settled and keep growing. https://enduringword.com/walking-rooted-building/ 
- Henry: the closer we walk with Christ, the more firmly rooted we become. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Col/Col_002.cfm 

**v. 8**
- Guzik: the false teaching presented itself as "traditional," but it carried man's stamp, not God's. https://enduringword.com/dont-get-cheated/  He describes it as a mix of early Gnosticism, Greek philosophy, mystery religions and Jewish mysticism. He also notes that commentators disagree about which element was strongest. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/colossians-2/
- Some take the "spiritual forces of the world" (*stoicheia*) to be spirits or elemental forces. If so, Paul is saying Christ is greater than any of them. https://enduringword.com/dont-get-cheated/ 
- Older commentators: Paul isn't condemning sound philosophy, only the baseless kind (Macknight, in Benson). Ellicott says these "traditions" came from human speculation and were passed on secretly to insiders. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/colossians/2-8.htm 
- Henry thinks it refers to Jewish ceremonies as well as pagan learning. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Col/Col_002.cfm 
- **Catholic view:** the Catholic Encyclopedia says only the false teachers' philosophy is condemned. It adds that "tradition of men" does not disparage apostolic traditions. https://www.catholic.com/encyclopedia/epistle-to-the-colossians  Guzik makes a similar distinction elsewhere, but for him the apostolic traditions are those preserved in the New Testament. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/2-thessalonians-2/ 

**v. 9**
- Guzik calls this an "airtight" statement that Jesus is fully God. "Bodily" counters the Gnostic split between spirit and matter. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/colossians-2/ 
- Henry reads "bodily" as the opposite of shadow, not of spirit: God's fullness lives in Christ really, not figuratively. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Col/Col_002.cfm 

**v. 10**
- Believers are complete in Christ only because He is truly God. Anything that says we are incomplete in Him takes away from His deity. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/colossians-2/ 
- Christ rules over all the spirit beings the false teachers made so much of. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/colossians-2/ 

**v. 11**
- Ellicott: "made without hands" has come to mean "spiritual." Following Chrysostom, he notes that physical circumcision removed a small part, while spiritual circumcision removes the whole power of the flesh. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/colossians/2-11.htm 
- Barnes: "circumcision of Christ" doesn't mean Christ's own circumcision. It is the kind He established, the renouncing of sin. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/colossians/2-11.htm 
- Gill: this circumcision of the heart is the Spirit's work, not man's or his free will. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/colossians/2-11.html 
- Peake, quoted by Guzik: the false teachers probably urged circumcision as a route to higher holiness, not as required for salvation. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/colossians-2/ 
- **Scholarly view:** one older critical commentary on the Bible Hub page (the Greek-text notes) cites Schneckenburger and others who read "circumcision of Christ" as Christ's death. This fits the burial and resurrection that follow. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/colossians/2-11.htm 

**v. 12 (the main point of Protestant disagreement)**
- **Baptist:** John Piper says this text kept him from accepting infant baptism. The real counterpart of circumcision is Christ's spiritual circumcision, and baptism is its outward expression. "Through faith" decides it: infants can't believe, so they aren't fit subjects. https://www.desiringgod.org/messages/buried-and-raised-in-baptism-through-faith  GotQuestions agrees: baptism follows spiritual circumcision rather than replacing it. https://www.gotquestions.org/baptism-circumcision.html 
- **Reformed/Presbyterian:** Kevin DeYoung says baptism and circumcision "carried the same spiritual import," so children shouldn't be left out of the sign. https://www.thegospelcoalition.org/blogs/kevin-deyoung/a-brief-defense-of-infant-baptism/  A Themelios article admits spiritual circumcision fulfils physical circumcision. It argues that baptism still replaces circumcision as the sign of that reality. https://www.thegospelcoalition.org/themelios/article/sacramental-supersessionism-revisited-a-response-to-martin-salter-on-the-re/  Calvin: Christ gives spiritual circumcision "not through means of that ancient sign... but by baptism." https://www.studylight.org/commentary/colossians/2-12.html 
- Ligonier calls baptism a means of grace for those who trust Christ. Citing the Westminster Confession, it says the grace isn't necessarily tied to the moment of baptism. Baptized infants receive it if and when they later believe. https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/faith-and-means-grace
- **Mode:** Gill says "buried" shows baptism was by full immersion. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/colossians/2-12.html 
- **Another view** (the "Contending for the Faith" commentary on StudyLight): Christ circumcises the heart at the moment of baptism. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/colossians/2-12.html 
- **Catholic:** Trent Horn argues baptism is better than circumcision because it "really does cleanse and change our souls." https://www.catholic.com/audio/cot/dialogue-answering-gavin-ortlunds-baptism-questions 
- Guzik (Pentecostal-leaning): baptism shows our identity in Jesus; it is not the same thing as circumcision. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/colossians-2/ 

**v. 13**
- Henry: sin is spiritual death, which is separation from God and an inability to help oneself. Christ's resurrection brings our souls to life, and forgiveness is that new life. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Col/Col_002.cfm 

**v. 14**
- Henry gives two readings of the "debt" or "decrees." It could be the curse of the moral law against sinners, or the ceremonial law that divided Jews from Gentiles. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Col/Col_002.cfm 
- Guzik: Jesus paid the debt and also removed the record so it can no longer accuse us. N.T. Wright pictures it as the charge notice nailed above the cross, put there by God rather than Pilate. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/colossians-2/ 

**v. 15**
- The paradox of the cross: the "defeated" Jesus stripped the spiritual powers and paraded them in public. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/colossians-2/  Henry calls it a victory over the powers of darkness. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Col/Col_002.cfm 

**v. 16 (disagreement over the Sabbath)**
- The "therefore" points back to the cross in vv. 13–15. https://enduringword.com/blog-archive/weekly-devotionals/shadows-and-substance/ 
- **Weekly Sabbath not binding:** Precept Austin says the weekly Sabbath is clearly in view and is no longer binding. https://www.preceptaustin.org/colossians_216-23  Schreiner (TGC) agrees and mentions the other view, that "Sabbath" here means sabbatical years. He says the New Testament doesn't say when Christians should rest. https://www.thegospelcoalition.org/blogs/justin-taylor/schreiner-qa-is-the-sabbath-still-required-for-christians/ 
- **Freedom either way:** GotQuestions says believers may keep a Sabbath, but shouldn't judge those who don't. https://www.gotquestions.org/Sabbath-keeping.html 
- **Catholic:** Catholics agree with Seventh-day Adventists that the third commandment still binds Christians, but not that the day must be the seventh. The old Sabbath is a "mere shadow," and the Lord's Day replaced it. https://www.catholic.com/magazine/print-edition/the-lords-day-replaced-the-sabbath 
- Precept Austin's material names Seventh-day Adventists as insisting on Sabbath-keeping. https://www.preceptaustin.org/pdf/59967/ 
- I found no source defending the Reformed "Christian Sabbath" (Westminster) reading.

**v. 17**
- The food laws, festivals and Sabbaths were God-given outlines that prepared for the Redeemer. https://biblehub.com/colossians/2-17.htm  Ellicott says these things foreshadowed Christ and are set aside now that He has come. https://biblehub.com/colossians/2-17.htm 
- Schreiner: Hebrews 10:1 uses the same word "shadow" for the Old Testament sacrifices. https://www.thegospelcoalition.org/blogs/justin-taylor/schreiner-qa-is-the-sabbath-still-required-for-christians/ 

**v. 18**
- Guzik: Gnosticism and some Jewish mysticism honoured angel-like go-betweens between God and the world, so Paul warns against worshipping angels. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/colossians-2/

**v. 20**
- The way out of legalism is remembering we died with Christ. Our union with His death and resurrection, not law-keeping, becomes the foundation of the Christian life. https://enduringword.com/do-not/ 

**v. 21**
- Legalistic religion is defined more by what we *don't* do than by what we do. Christianity has clear moral limits, but at heart it is about positive action. https://enduringword.com/do-not/ 

**v. 22**
- Rule-keeping centres on temporary things, not the realities that matter most. https://enduringword.com/do-not/ 

**v. 23**
- Legalism can't hold back sin. It feeds spiritual pride and misses that we died to the old system. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/colossians-2/
